newsitem.title: CHINA: Maanshan sees flat profit despite share rally.
newsitem.headline: Maanshan sees flat profit despite share rally.

text.p: Maanshan Iron & Steel, whose shares have rallied on the Shanghai exchange in the past few days, said on Thursday profit this year will outperform last year but still remain well behind 1994 results.
Maanshan, China's biggest supplier of iron and steel for construction use, closed at 3.82 yuan on volume of 81.1 million shares on Thursday, up 23.6 percent from last Thursday's 3.09 yuan.
Analysts said domestic institutions had been buying Maanshan as part of an effort to boost the A index in order to attract fresh capital into the stock market.
Maanshan, which has the second-largest number of shares outstanding on the Shanghai stock market, had a relatively big impact on the movement of the index, they said.
But a company official said the company was not optimistic about its 1996 profits as a result of rising prices of raw materials, a weak steel market and a cut in the export tax rebate rate.
"The situation is a little better than last year, but it is hard to reach the 1994 level with demand still weak," he said.

The export tax rebate for which Maanshan is eligible was cut at the beginning of this year to nine percent from 14 percent, with a negative impact of 23 million yuan on the company's first-half results, he added.
In the first half of 1996, the company posted a net profit of 35 million yuan, down from 40 million in the same 1995 period.
The official declined to forecast a full 1996 profit but he said profit in the second half-year will be a little more than that in the first half.
The company posted a net profit of 43.2 million yuan in 1995, down 94.2 percent from 749 million in 1994.
